time. It reports aggregate money only and deliberately carries no

time whose contributor has no rate on record is reported separately as
uncosted rather than silently folded in as zero-cost work.

cost_minor_units is the labour cost of billable logged time in the
smallest unit of the business currency, so no rounding happens before
the caller sees it.

costed_minutes.description:
costed_minutes is billable logged time whose contributor had a rate on
record; it is the time included in cost_minor_units.

project_id.description: project_id is the project the cost was computed for.

uncosted_employee_count is how many distinct contributors have no rate
on record.

uncosted_minutes.description:
uncosted_minutes is billable logged time whose contributor has no rate
on record. A total with uncosted_minutes above zero understates true
labour cost and must be labelled as partial where it is displayed.

flow.status.v2.Status.description:
Status is one entry in a project's own status set.

Versioned v2 rather than v1 despite being a new capability. Every live flow
capability is on v2 after the workspace removal, and v1 contracts are still
being deleted, so a lone `flow/status/v1` would read as the older of two
generations when it is the only one that exists. Nothing here has a v1
history to be compatible with.

A project with no statuses is the normal case, not an unconfigured one. It
falls back to the six built-in string statuses, which is what makes the whole
feature additive.

bucket.description:
bucket is the semantic meaning, one of "backlog", "active", "done" or
"cancelled".

It exists so a rollup can count across projects whose pipelines have
nothing in common: a project calling its in-flight state "Building" and
one calling it "Legal review" both report `active`.

The contract cannot express a closed set, so the server validates it and
rejects anything else with 400. Do not treat an unrecognised value as a
default; that is how a cancelled task would get counted as open.

"in_review", "done" or "cancelled".

The string status column is not going away, so every existing query,
filter and index keeps working and no consumer has to learn about this
capability to stay correct. A custom status reports its nearest built-in.

was @required for exactly that reason and it made every update to an active
employee silently impossible.

lines of work inside it, and the work-type tree those lines are classified by.

either level; hr_category_id maps the node onto HR's payroll category so one
entry serves both project reporting and payroll.

hr.shift.v1.AvailabilityPayload.description:
AvailabilityPayload is one window in which a staff member can, or explicitly
cannot, be scheduled for a shift. A row is either a recurring weekly pattern
(day_of_week set, specific_date absent) or a single-date override
(specific_date set, day_of_week absent); an override takes precedence over the
recurring pattern for the date it names.

Exactly one of day_of_week and specific_date is set on every stored row. .onk
has no cross-field decorator for that constraint (the same gap documented on
flow.task.v1.ListTasksRequest), so it is enforced in the onion handler rather
than in this schema.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp when this entry was created.

day_of_week.description:
Weekday of a recurring pattern: 0 = Monday through 6 = Sunday. Absent on a
single-date override. Numbered Monday-first so the value indexes the same
week the roster already uses (GetRosterRequest.week_start is a Monday).
This is deliberately not JavaScript's Date.getDay(), where 0 = Sunday.

end_time.description:
End of the window (HH:MM 24-hour format). An end_time earlier than
start_time means the window crosses midnight and ends the following day,
which is how availability for a night shift is expressed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the availability entry.

is_available.description:
Whether the staff member can be scheduled in this window. False marks a
deliberate block, which is how a single-date override withdraws
availability that the recurring pattern would otherwise grant.
Wire note: the generated Go server tags every scalar `omitempty`, so a
false value is dropped from the response body. Read an absent key as false.

owner_id.description: Tenant owner this entry belongs to.

specific_date.description:
Calendar date a single-date override applies to (ISO-8601, e.g.
"2026-08-17"). Absent on a recurring pattern.

staff_id.description:
Staff member whose availability this is. Matches ShiftPayload.staff_id, not
the older ShiftAssignmentPayload.employee_id in this same package.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp when this entry was last updated.

date.description: Date of the assignment (ISO-8601 date).

employee_id.description: Employee to assign.

warnings.description:
Human-readable availability warnings raised against the assignee for this
date (e.g. "Jane Doe is unavailable 09:00-12:00 on 2026-08-20"), read off
the AvailabilityPayload rows in this package.

Advisory only. The assignment is still created, because a scheduler
legitimately needs to staff someone against a stated preference: cover for
a no-show, a swap the pair agreed offline, a rush the roster did not
anticipate. A hard block would make those ordinary cases impossible
without first editing the availability record, so the check informs rather
than refuses. Empty when no conflict was found.

Mirrors GetRosterResponse.conflicts, which already reports this class of
problem the same non-blocking way.

producing a duplicate. start_time belongs to that key so one staff member can
hold several windows on the same day, for example a split shift of 09:00 to
12:00 and 14:00 to 18:00.

request carrying both or neither.

would silently block the window.
